title: Tensor with globally strict-perfect coefficient sheaves preserves countable products
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, and let $A_T$ be the ring sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Work in $D=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T))$, with the countable derived products of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. Let $E\in D$ admit a bounded complex representative $E^\bullet$ such that every $E^j$ is a direct summand of $A_T^{N_j}$ for some finite integer $N_j$. For every countable family $(C_n)_{n\geq1}$ of objects of $D$, the canonical comparison induced by the product projections
$$
(R\!\prod_{n\geq1}C_n)\otimes_{A_T}^LE\longrightarrow R\!\prod_{n\geq1}(C_n\otimes_{A_T}^LE)
$$
is an isomorphism, functorially in $E$ and the family.

source.place: proof, final sentence on tensor and the two Roos products; global bounded finite-projective mechanism, interpreted in the A_T-module sheaf category

proof.text: Choose the given bounded representative E^\bullet and complex representatives I_n of C_n. A bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free A_T-modules is K-flat: tensoring an acyclic complex with a finite free complex is acyclic degreewise, and the property is preserved by finite direct sums, bounded totalization, and retracts. Hence E^\bullet\otimes_{A_T}I_n computes C_n\otimes^L_{A_T}E. By the termwise product description in [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], which applies because countable products are exact, the product complex \prod_n I_n represents R\!\prod_n C_n. The canonical comparison is therefore represented by the chain map (\prod_n I_n)\otimes E^\bullet\to\prod_n(I_n\otimes E^\bullet), with all objects in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T)).

source.place: proof, final sentence: tensor with the bounded finite-projective representative in the A_T-module sheaf category

proof.text: For a finite free term A_T^r, tensoring a product of complexes with that term is the canonical finite distributivity map (\prod_n C_n)^r\cong\prod_n C_n^r. The same map is an isomorphism for a direct summand, because the idempotent defining the summand acts on both sides and the product comparison intertwines these idempotents. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism degreewise for every term E^j, and it is natural in the term maps and in the family maps.

source.place: proof, bounded finite-projective mechanism: finite free terms and direct summands

proof.text: Since E^\bullet is bounded, each degree of its total tensor with a product is a finite direct sum of the degreewise comparisons from step 2. These finite direct sums are isomorphisms, and the displayed sign differential is respected because every component comparison is induced by the same product projections. Hence the chain map is a quasi-isomorphism before passing to the derived category. The exactness of countable products of A_T-module sheaves ensures that the product complex represents the derived product and that this quasi-isomorphism remains an isomorphism after localization.

source.place: proof, Roos product computation: finite totalization and exact countable products

proof.text: By the definition of the derived inverse-limit construction, each occurrence R\!\prod_{n\geq1}C_n is the product in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T)) computed termwise by the exact-product model. Applying the chain-level isomorphism of step 3 and then localizing gives the canonical comparison in the statement. Because every map used is induced by the projections and the tensor bifunctor, the construction is functorial in E and in all maps of the family (C_n).
